clue.text: Butterfly operating all over the place

indicators.note: scattered all over the place, so the letters of the preceding word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A butterfly flits about busily wherever it goes.
explanation.definitionFit: The orange-tip is a common European butterfly whose males have bright orange wingtips.

clue.text: Hollywood success means nothing to Mark

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
a scar is a mark left on the skin

explanation.surface: A film star shrugs off winning a top award as trivial.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oscar is an Academy Award, the top prize of the American film industry.

clue.text: Awakening of love in Laura's development

indicators.note: the love letter goes inside the rearranged name
a development of the name means it is reworked into another arrangement

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A girl named Laura grows up and discovers romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'development' turns LAURAS into ARUSAL, with O placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Arousal is the act of waking or stirring someone, an awakening.

clue.text: Information given to us in class

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
taken as written

explanation.surface: A teacher hands out facts to pupils in a lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology a genus is a class or group of related species.

clue.text: Staff upset about rising Inland Revenue taxes

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the other piece
upset means knocked over or disordered, so the letters are jumbled
in a down clue, rising means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: IR is the abbreviation for the former UK tax authority, the Inland Revenue

explanation.surface: Employees are angry about higher taxes from the authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: Inland Revenue was the old name of the UK tax office; in a down clue the reversed piece reads upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Tariffs are duties or levies charged on goods, a form of tax.

clue.text: Pursue writing style attractive to Americans

parts.note: prose is ordinary written language, as opposed to verse
cute is the American usage for attractive

explanation.surface: Someone chases a style of writing that appeals in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: To prosecute a task is to pursue or carry it on; also to bring legal proceedings.

clue.text: The lure of old-fashioned sex appeal to some degree

indicators.note: the sex appeal piece is added to the degree piece, which comes first

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a university degree
IT was 1920s slang for sex appeal, as in the 'It girl' Clara Bow

explanation.surface: A mild allure of vintage charm, only partly effective.
explanation.walkthrough: IT for sex appeal is dated slang, hence 'old-fashioned'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bait is something offered to entice a fish or a person, a synonym for a lure.

clue.text: He may call for you at a hotel in New York

definitions.text: He may call for you at a hotel in New York

parts.words: He may call for you at a hotel in New York
parts.note: suggests a visitor collecting you, but means a hotel porter who answers a call for service

explanation.walkthrough: The term is American, hence New York.
explanation.definitionFit: A bellhop is a US hotel porter who carries bags and runs errands for guests.

clue.text: Popular officer, on the whole

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a general is a senior army officer

explanation.surface: A well-liked commander is generally approved of.
explanation.definitionFit: In general means usually or broadly speaking, an idiom matching on the whole.

clue.text: Drinking vessel

parts.note: reads as a cup or glass, but also a ship (vessel) that is drinking, i.e. sailing the sea

explanation.definitionFit: A schooner is both a tall glass for sherry or beer and a two-masted sailing ship.

clue.text: Accommodate to do a favour

definitions.meaning: to accommodate someone is to meet their needs
to help someone out as a kindness

explanation.definitionFit: To oblige means both to accommodate someone's wishes and to do them a kindness.

clue.text: Many pay increases result in difficulties

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100, a crossword stand-in for many
rises are increases in pay

explanation.surface: Lots of wage hikes cause economic trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Crises are times of serious trouble or emergencies, plural like the definition.

clue.text: Let the workman go without guidance

parts.note: to let go is to free
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: An employer dismisses a labourer with no direction given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let ... go' gives FREE; 'go' completes the phrase and supplies no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing freehand means drawing without rulers or other guiding instruments.

clue.text: A new film about a tourist resort in Italy

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the second a
a new version of the word film, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recent movie is set in a popular Italian holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns FILM into MLFI, and 'about' wraps that round the second A to give MALFI, after the opening A.
explanation.definitionFit: Amalfi is a town on the Amalfi Coast south of Naples, a famous holiday destination.

clue.text: Order retreat

definitions.meaning: a religious order's community and its house
a place of seclusion and quiet

explanation.definitionFit: A monastery houses a religious order and is a secluded place of withdrawal from the world.

clue.text: Aware how Kent got into difficulties, when batting first

indicators.note: this piece is placed at the front of the answer

parts.note: a batsman at the crease is in

indicators.note: the words how and Kent fall into disorder, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A commentator explains how the Kent cricket team collapsed once batting.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is an English county with a cricket team. 'got into difficulties' turns HOW and KENT into THEKNOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in the know is well informed, aware of inside information.

clue.text: Put a foot wrong and they may bail you out!

definitions.text: Put a foot wrong and they may bail you out!

parts.words: Put a foot wrong and they may bail you out!
parts.note: in cricket a batsman whose foot strays out of the crease can be stumped by the wicketkeeper, who knocks the bails off; it reads like rescue from jail

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the bails are the small crosspieces on the stumps; a wicketkeeper knocks them off to get out a batsman who has left his ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Stumpers is an informal word for wicketkeepers, who dismiss batsmen by stumping.

clue.text: Discovers her aunt's in trouble

indicators.note: something in trouble is in disarray, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone finds out that a relative is having difficulties.
explanation.definitionFit: To unearth something is to dig it up or bring it to light, so to discover it.

clue.text: Articles on writing music

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
the is the definite article
MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: Published pieces about written scores and songs.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthems are songs of praise or patriotism, pieces of music.

clue.text: A double rum is put out for Eastern fighters

indicators.note: put out means disturbed, so the letters are rearranged
a double of the letter A means writing it twice

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bartender serves a double measure of rum to warriors from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' rearranges AA, RUM and IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Samurai were the warrior class of feudal Japan, fighters from the Far East.

clue.text: They play supporting roles in the studio

definitions.text: They play supporting roles in the studio

parts.words: They play supporting roles in the studio
parts.note: sounds like minor actors, but means stands that literally support canvases in an artist's studio

explanation.definitionFit: Easels are wooden frames that hold an artist's canvas upright while painting.

clue.text: She is used to getting high scores

definitions.text: She is used to getting high scores

parts.words: She is used to getting high scores
parts.note: sounds like a top-scoring player, but means a singer given the highest notes in a musical score

explanation.definitionFit: A soprano is the highest female singing voice and the singer who has it.

clue.text: A hotline to the weatherman

parts.note: suggests a direct phone link, but means a line on a weather map joining places of equal temperature

explanation.definitionFit: On meteorological maps, lines linking points of equal temperature have this name.

clue.text: Please request a re-trial

definitions.meaning: to please is to attract or charm
to ask a higher court to reverse a verdict

explanation.definitionFit: Appeal means both to be attractive to someone and to ask a higher court to review a case.

clue.text: Acknowledge head of music in entrance

indicators.note: the picked letter goes inside the entrance word

parts.note: an adit is a horizontal entrance to a mine

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The conductor admits the lead musician was in the doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit something is to confess or concede it, to acknowledge it.

clue.text: Wide awake to a siren call

definitions.meaning: a warning signal sounded by a siren

explanation.definitionFit: Alert means watchful, and as a noun an alarm warning, such as an air-raid siren.

clue.text: Lower form emend a composition

indicators.note: a composition is a putting-together, so the words emend and a are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A junior school class is told to correct a piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower form' reads as a junior class, but only 'Lower' defines; 'form' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To demean someone is to degrade them, to bring them down in dignity.

clue.text: Runs riot after the beak leaves

parts.note: a ram is the beak-like projection on an old warship's prow
the leaves of a book are its pages

explanation.surface: Wild behaviour breaks out once the magistrate has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beak' is British slang for a magistrate, which the surface exploits.
explanation.definitionFit: To rampage is to rush about violently, out of control.

clue.text: A word of agreement — or more than one

definitions.text: A word of agreement — or more than one

parts.words: A word of agreement — or more than one
parts.note: the singular word of assent, made plural for votes in favour

explanation.definitionFit: Ayes are votes in favour, plural of the old word for yes.

clue.text: Wait outside Ascot for a change of clothing

indicators.note: the first word sits on the outside of the other letters
the word Ascot is changed, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone waits by the racecourse to change outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal Ascot is an English horse race where formal dress is worn, so the surface suggests a change of outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: A waistcoat is a sleeveless garment worn under a jacket, an item of attire.
